text:
Ava (support): Heads-up — paying customer (AcmePayments) opened a support escalation. Their svc is seeing p95/p99 token latency spikes starting ~09:10 UTC and requests are timing out for some flows. They're on a Dedicated pool (eu-west-1, pool-id: dp-09).
Jon (eng-sre): Thanks. Do we have SLO alerts firing?
oncall-bot: Alert: dedicated_pool_latency_high - dp-09 - p95 1.8s (threshold 1.0s) - triggered at 2026-03-15T09:12:02Z
deploy-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-8423 (assigned to eng-sre)
Ava (support): Customer reports errors: `504 gateway timeout` and occasional `429` during retries. They attempted 3 retries then gave up.
Mia (customer-success): They're high-value — asking for ETA. Can we prioritize?
Carlos (oncall): I'm paged, grabbing logs. Initial look: pool dp-09 shows provisioning events and many cold starts.
Priya (eng-runtime): On it — pulling runtime metrics and autoscaler events. Could be scale-up lag or scheduler backlog.
Jon (eng-sre): Key things to confirm: 1) autoscaler decisions (requested vs ready GPUs) 2) pending pods/containers 3) KV cache hit rate and model size fallback behavior.
Priya (eng-runtime): Dashboards: https://console.redwood.internal/dp/dp-09/overview - p95 jump aligns with a spike in pending container creation at 09:09-09:14 UTC. Also saw repeated `CreateContainer` retries with `insufficient_gpus` from the scheduler.
Ava (support): Customer says traffic spiked by ~2.5x due to a campaign — expected, but their commit is supposed to cover baseline + 2x burst.
Jon (eng-sre): Do we have capacity headroom? Check reserved vs burst config.
Priya (eng-runtime): Config for dp-09: reserved=40 GPUs, burstable=8, autoscale.min=40, autoscale.max=72. Right now node pool at 40, requested peaked to ~64 GPUs. Cluster couldn't schedule additional GPUs because the cloud provider took 4-6m to attach new GPU instances.
Carlos (oncall): That explains scale-up lag. Cold start time for GPU instances was 220s median in the timeline — longer than usual (normal ~90s). Something in the provisioning provider region is delayed.
Jon (eng-sre): Any evictions or resource fragmentation?
Priya (eng-runtime): We saw fragmentation: several mid-size instances left unusable for single-GPU pods because of pod anti-affinity rules. Also our warmup controller (warmers) had been disabled for dp-09 due to a previous cost-optimization experiment.
Ava (support): So two problems: provider attach delay + warmers disabled -> more cold GPU starts -> p95/p99 spike. Customer wants mitigation now.
Mia (customer-success): They've asked for temporary routing to hosted API while we fix; they agreed to revert to hosted for burst traffic but want TLS+data isolation confirmation.
Jon (eng-sre): Short term mitigations we can do now: 1) enable warmers for dp-09 (pre-warm a few instances), 2) temporarily relax anti-affinity so smaller pods can pack, 3) increase burst capacity if available, 4) route canary traffic to hosted model instance. Which are safe to do quickly?
Priya (eng-runtime): I'll enable warmers and relax anti-affinity for 10m window. Steps:
```bash
# enable warmers
redwoodctl pools update dp-09 --warmers=on --warm-count=6
# relax anti-affinity
redwoodctl pools update dp-09 --affinity=relaxed --affinity-duration=600
```
Applying now.
deploy-bot: change queued: dp-09 warmers=on, affinity=relaxed — rollout started
Priya (eng-runtime): Warmers request acked; warmers started booting pre-provisioned image. Expected warm-up time ~60-90s for warmed images.
Carlos (oncall): Also triggered cloud provider support SLA ticket — they reported degraded attach times in eu-west-1 zone b.
Jon (eng-sre): Can we adjust autoscaler aggressiveness to request nodes earlier? Possibly lower `scale_up_cooldown` and increase `scale_target` to be proactive. But this risks overshoot/cost.
Priya (eng-runtime): I'll lower scale_up_cooldown from 120s to 30s for dp-09 and set target_utilization to 60% to request capacity sooner. Command: `redwoodctl autoscale update dp-09 --scale-up-cooldown=30 --target-util=0.6`
Ava (support): I told the customer we'd try routing their burst to hosted while we confirm warmers working — they approved.
Jon (eng-sre): Who can run a quick smoke test once warmers report healthy? Need to validate latency at p95 before telling customer it's resolved.
Priya (eng-runtime): Warmers reported HEALTHY at 09:18:05 UTC. Running a synthetic at 10 rps for 2 minutes against their workload profile (seq length ~512) now.
Priya (eng-runtime): Smoke results (local): p50 180ms, p95 840ms, p99 1.5s — improvement vs 09:10 where p95 was 1.8s. Still borderline but much better.
Carlos (oncall): Cloud provider has a patch ETA ~45m; but our warmers + autoscale changes should mitigate immediate customer impact.
Mia (customer-success): Customer switched burst to hosted routing, saw immediate reduction in errors. They asked for postmortem later and wanted suggestions to avoid recurrence.
Jon (eng-sre): Action items for post-incident: 1) revert the cost experiment that disabled warmers (dp-09 exception) 2) add a pre-provisioning policy for critical customers (pin a small warm buffer) 3) improve fragmentation handling (bin-packing optimizer) 4) add synthetic canary for autoscale latency (measure attach latency trend) 5) document runbook for hosted fallback (privately routable)
Ava (support): I'll file a customer-facing summary and ETA for follow-up.
Priya (eng-runtime): I'll keep dp-09 warmers on for next 2h and monitor attach times/latency. Rolling config diff applied.
Jon (eng-sre): Also add metric alert for `provider_attach_time_median` and threshold >120s.
oncall-bot: Alert resolved: dedicated_pool_latency_high - dp-09 - cleared at 2026-03-15T09:21:12Z
Ava (support): Customer confirmed error rate dropped to near 0.5% and happy with hosted fallback. They'll await the postmortem. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
Carlos (oncall): Leaving this thread open for the postmortem notes and follow-ups.
Priya (eng-runtime): Quick repro steps (for postmortem):
1) Simulate 2.5x traffic spike against dp-09 model endpoint using `ab` with payload from customer's template.
2) Monitor `node_attach_time`, `pending_containers`, `warmers_active` and `kv_cache_hit_rate`.
3) Observe autoscaler request -> provider attach delays -> cold start ratio increase -> p95 spike.

Example load command:
```bash
ab -n 10000 -c 50 -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -T "application/json" -p /tmp/payload.json https://dp-09.redwood/api/v1/generate
```
Jon (eng-sre): I'll draft the postmortem with timeline + root cause + mitigations. Will include config diffs and a recommendation to add warm-buffer SLAs for dedicated customers.
Mia (customer-success): Thanks. I'll schedule a 1:1 with AcmePayments to review and share timeline once postmortem ready.
Ava (support): Closing updates — will keep thread for notes.
